_comment: US-2389 SHARED FIXTURE. 'Which REQUIRED eBay aspects are still unfilled' is computed by TWO implementations that cannot import each other: services/edge-functions/src/lib/aspect-provenance.ts (requiredMissingAspects) and src/lib/aspect-provenance.ts (requiredMissingAspectNames). The edge copy is the PUBLISH BLOCKER -- it decides the 422 that stops a publish or revise and names the missing aspects. The web copy is the pre-publish CHECKLIST the seller sees in the composer. vault/30-platform/ebay-required-aspect-completeness.md used to claim they were 'the same helper ... so the UI warning and the server blocker cannot disagree'. They are two copies, so they can. If the checklist says a listing is ready and the blocker refuses it, the seller has no way to find out what is wrong -- the UI is telling them nothing is missing. Both suites assert THIS table, which is the same remedy US-2034 used for the weighted-overall mirrors and US-1995 for title-sync. NOTE ON SHAPES: the edge type makes aspectConstraint optional and the web type makes it required, so the web runner casts. That difference is itself a drift risk and is why case 'missing-constraint-object' exists -- it is the input on which the two types disagree, and both implementations must still return the same answer.

cases.why: the ordinary case: one required aspect filled, one required aspect empty
an OPTIONAL aspect with no value is not missing -- only required ones block a publish
an EMPTY ARRAY counts as unfilled, not as filled. This is the shape a cleared field leaves behind, and treating it as filled would let a publish through that eBay then rejects
a required aspect absent from the values map entirely

missing-constraint-object: the aspect spec has no aspectConstraint at all. The two TYPES disagree about whether this is representable (edge optional, web required), so it is exactly the input where a drift would hide. Not required means not missing
a required aspect with a BLANK NAME is skipped rather than reported as an empty-string requirement, which would render as a nameless bullet in the seller's checklist and a nameless entry in the 422
no localizedAspectName key at all -- same skip as a blank name
ORDER follows the category spec, not the values map. The seller reads this list top to bottom against the form, so a reordering is a real regression even though the set is unchanged
an empty aspect list yields nothing missing -- an uncategorised item is not 'complete', but that is the category picker's problem, not this rule's
